item.title: A prime isoartinian ring that is not noetherian
item.description: arXiv:2610.23129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A right module is isoartinian (resp., isonoetherian) if every descending (resp., ascending) chain of submodules is eventually constant up to isomorphism, and a ring R is right isoartinian (resp., isonoethe- rian) if RR is isoartinian (resp., isonoetherian). Facchini and Nazemian proved that a semiprime right isoartinian ring is right noetherian if and only if it is right isonoetherian if and only if it has finite Goldie dimen- sion and that every commutative semiprime isoartinian ring is noether- ian. We construct, over an arbitrary field K, a (non commutative) prime (right and left) isoartinian ring that is neither right nor left noetherian.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Nazemian, Doniyor Yazdonov

item.title: Generalized Mock-Poisson Algebras: Constructions and Structural Properties
item.description: arXiv:2610.23143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce generalized mock-Poisson algebras as a mock analogue of generalized Poisson algebras. We prove that $A_\ast^3$ is an ideal annihilated by both operations and that the quotient $A/A_\ast^3$ is a mock-Poisson algebra. We also show that the dimension seven is the smallest dimension in which a generalized mock-Poisson algebra need not be a mock-Poisson algebra. We give several constructions using derivations, anti-Zinbiel algebras, tensor products, and one-dimensional extensions. We study polarization and depolarization and characterize the corresponding admissible algebras. We prove that every finite-dimensional generalized mock-Poisson algebra over a field of characteristic zero is nilpotent. Finally, we describe representations in terms of semidirect products.
item.dc:creator: Zafar Normatov

item.title: Point Modules of Non-Connected Graded Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As part of a program to extend the homogeneous coordinate ring techniques of Artin-Tate-Van den Bergh to twisted graded Calabi-Yau (tCY) algebras, we initiate the study of point modules of non-connected graded algebras. We define weak and strong point modules of graded quotients of path algebras and compute their respective moduli stacks. We describe the relation between these point stacks and the classical point schemes in the connected graded setting, and we analyze the point stacks of several 2 and 3-dimensional tCY algebras.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Lamkin

item.title: On the center of the Clifford Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.23323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The center of a Clifford algebra associated to a non-degenerate quadratic form over a field is described in the existing literature, but an elementary proof of the result seems lacking. The aim of this paper is to provide such an elementary proof.
item.dc:creator: Chris Peters, Hans Sterk

item.title: The algebraic and geometric classification of semi-alternative superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The algebraic and geometric classifications of complex $3$-dimensional semi-alternative superalgebras are given. As corollaries, we obtain the algebraic and geometric classifications of complex $3$-dimensional $\mathfrak{perm}$, associative, and assosymmetric superalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Hani Abdelwahab, Ivan Kaygorodov, Roman Lubkov

item.title: Quasi-derivations of the (extended) Schr\"odinger--Witt algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Schr\"odinger--Witt algebras are infinite-dimensional Lie algebras of local dynamical symmetries of the free Schr\"odinger equation; they contain the Witt algebra of conformal transformations of the time line and appear in non-equilibrium statistical physics and in non-relativistic conformal field theory. We describe all quasi-derivations of the original and the twisted Schr\"odinger--Witt algebras. We prove that every quasi-derivation is the sum of a derivation, a trivial $\frac12$-derivation, a linear map with values in the center, and a finite linear combination of maps from three new families of quasi-derivations. As corollaries, we describe all $\delta$-derivations, all $\delta$-biderivations and all transposed $\delta$-Poisson structures of the Schr\"odinger--Witt algebras. Finally, we prove that every quasi-derivation of the (original or twisted) extended Schr\"odinger--Witt algebra is the sum of an inner derivation and a multiple of the identity map. As a consequence, there are no nontrivial $\delta$-derivations (for $\delta\notin \{\frac12,1\}$), $\delta$-biderivations (for $\delta\neq1$), and transposed $\delta$-Poisson structures on these algebras.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Kaygorodov, Abror Khudoyberdiyev, Zarina Shermatova

item.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.23684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by P\'olya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.
item.dc:creator: Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: Transposed Poisson structures in graded and algebroid geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.22629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We ask whether the transposed Leibniz rule $2z\cdot[x,y]=[z\cdot x,y]+[x,z\cdot y]$ survives the two passages that turn Poisson algebras into geometry, the shift of degree which produces Gerstenhaber algebras and the passage from algebras to algebroids. We introduce graded transposed Poisson algebras with a bracket of arbitrary degree and show that the parity of the degree decides which shape the answer takes. In even degree, over a unital base, such brackets are in bijection with homogeneous derivations, and on the exterior algebra of a vector bundle in degree zero they are exactly the gauge derivations of the bundle. In odd degree the bracket is forced to be the product with a single element of that degree, so a non-negatively graded algebra carries no non-zero transposed Gerstenhaber bracket. In particular, for a Lie--Rinehart algebra $(A,L)$, the Schouten--Rinehart Gerstenhaber algebra $\Lambda_A L$ is transposed if and only if the anchor and the bracket of $L$ both vanish. We then introduce transposed $F$-algebroids and classify those with an identity: if the rank is at least two the anchor vanishes and the structure is the datum of a derivation of the multiplication, while if the rank is one the bundle is trivialised by the identity and the structure is, globally, the Jacobi bracket of a single vector field. For the tangent $F$-algebroid of an $F$-manifold $M$ this forces $\dim M=1$.
item.dc:creator: Gianmarco La Rosa

item.title: A monoid-theoretical approach to infinite direct-sum decompositions of modules
item.description: arXiv:2401.08203v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal C$ be a class of modules over a ring $R$, closed under direct sums over index sets of cardinality $\kappa$ and isomorphisms, and such that the isomorphism classes form a set. The monoid of modules $V(\mathcal C)$ encodes the behavior of finite direct-sum decompositions of modules in $\mathcal C$. We endow $V(\mathcal C)$ with an additional operation reflecting $\kappa$-indexed direct sums, and study the resulting $\kappa$-monoid $V^{\kappa}(\mathcal C)$. The braiding-property and an equivalent universal property, allow us to show: if every module in $\mathcal C$ is a direct sum of at most $\kappa$ many modules generated by strictly fewer than $\lambda$ many elements, then all relations on $V^{\kappa}(\mathcal C)$ are induced by relations between direct sums indexed by sets of cardinality strictly less than $\lambda$. A theorem of Kaplansky states that every projective module is a direct sum of countably generated modules. We show that also all relations between infinite direct sums of projective modules are induced from those between countable direct sums of countably generated projective modules. If every projective module over a ring $R$ is a direct sum of finitely generated projective modules, then the monoid of finitely generated projective modules $V(R)$ completely determines the $\kappa$-monoid $V^{\kappa}(R)$. Together with the realization result of Bergman and Dicks, this characterizes the $\kappa$-monoids appearing as $V^{\kappa}(R)$ for a hereditary ring. In general, the $\aleph_0$-monoid $V^{\aleph_0}(R)$ fully determines $V^{\kappa}(R)$. Herbera and P\v{r}\'ihoda's characterization of monoids of countably generated projective modules $V^*(R)$ over semilocal noetherian rings, yields a characterization of $V^{\kappa}(R)$ for these rings. We also characterize two-generated $\aleph_0$-monoids that appear as $V^{\aleph_0}(R)$ for hereditary rings $R$.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Nazemian, Daniel Smertnig

item.title: Classical Yang-Baxter equations and Nijenhuis operators for Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2502.18717v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper the conditions that when a Lie algebra is Nijenhuis are investigated. Furthermore all the Nijenhuis operators on $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ under the standard Cartan-Weyl basis are given. On the other hand, the relations between the classical Yang-Baxter equation and Nijenhuis operators $N$ on a Lie algebra and $P$ on a Lie coalgebra are derived by means of the bialgebraic theory for Nijenhuis Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Haiying Li, Tianshui Ma

item.title: Bialgebras induced by special left Alia algebras
item.description: arXiv:2506.07061v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates bialgebraic structures associated with special left-Alia algebras. Based on the special left-Alia algebras originally introduced in the study of algebras with skew-symmetric identity of degree 3, we systematically examine the structure of a Nijenhuis left-Alia bialgebra. This bialgebra consists of a compatible pairing between a Nijenhuis left-Alia algebra and a Nijenhuis left-Alia coalgebra. We prove that a Nijenhuis special left-Alia bialgebra, which is constructed from a commutative associative algebra (or a cocommutative coassociative coalgebra) equipped with two commuting linear maps, can be induced from a Nijenhuis commutative cocommutative associative D-bialgebra. This establishes an explicit link between these two families of bialgebraic structures. Furthermore, the paper provides a general method for constructing Nijenhuis operators on arbitrary left-Alia algebras and coalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Tianshui Ma, Chan Zhao, Huihui Zheng

item.title: Symmetric Rota-Baxter systems and applications
item.description: arXiv:2602.20631v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rota-Baxter operators and bialgebras are closely connected in several applications, such as the Connes-Kreimer renormalization framework and the operator approach to the classical Yang-Baxter equation. The concept of a Rota-Baxter system was introduced in 2016 as a generalization of a Rota-Baxter operator. In this work, we introduce a bialgebra structure compatible with a symmetric Rota-Baxter system, called a symmetric Rota-Baxter antisymmetric infinitesimal (ASI) bisystem. This bialgebra is characterized by generalizations of matched pairs of algebras and double constructions of Frobenius algebras to the setting of symmetric Rota-Baxter systems. Investigating the coboundary case leads to an enriched version of the associative Yang-Baxter equation (aYBe) adapted to symmetric Rota-Baxter systems. Antisymmetric solutions of this equation are used to construct symmetric Rota-Baxter ASI bisystems. We also introduce the notion of an $\mathcal{O}$-operator on a symmetric Rota-Baxter system, which produces solutions of the admissible aYBe in such systems and thereby gives rise to symmetric Rota-Baxter ASI bisystems. A symmetric Rota-Baxter bisystem generalizes several known structures, including Rota-Baxter Lie bisystems, Rota-Baxter ASI bialgebras, Rota-Baxter Lie bialgebras, averaging ASI bialgebras, averaging Lie bialgebras, and special apre-perm bialgebras.
item.dc:creator: Chan Zhao, Haiying Li, Tianshui Ma

item.title: Reynolds Leibniz bialgebras of any weight
item.description: arXiv:2603.19749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies bialgebraic structures associated with a Reynolds Leibniz algebra of weight $\lambda$, that is, a Leibniz algebra equipped with a Reynolds operator of weight $\lambda$. We first present equivalent characterizations of Reynolds Leibniz bialgebras of weight $\lambda$, using matched pairs and Manin triples. Next, we examine compatibility conditions between solutions of the classical Leibniz Yang-Baxter equation and Reynolds operators of weight $\lambda$, framed in terms of triangular Reynolds Leibniz bialgebras. Finally, building on results of Ayupov {\em et al.}, we classify two-dimensional triangular Reynolds Leibniz bialgebras of weight $\lambda$.
item.dc:creator: Tianshui Ma, Yuguang Ming, Chan Zhao

item.title: An Alternative Framework for Irreducibility and Primitivity of Nonnegative Tensors
item.description: arXiv:2606.30482v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by some recent studies on higher order Markov chains and well-known characterizations for irreducibility and primitivity of nonnegative matrices, we propose in this paper an alternative framework for irreducibility and primitivity of nonnegative tensors, giving rise to two new notions: s-irreducibility and s-primitivity. Our framework includes the relevant results on nonnegative matrices as its special cases, yet it expands existing results regarding irreducibility and primitivity of nonnegative tensors. In addition to its tensor theoretic significance, such a framework has important implications for applied problems such as higher order Markov chains.
item.dc:creator: Jianhong Xu

item.title: General Polynomials and Eigenvalues Over Cayley--Dickson Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.23613v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide an explicit method for determining the zero set of monic quadratic general polynomials over Cayley--Dickson algebras with any base field of characteristic not equal to $2$, which reduces the problem to finding the roots of univariate polynomials over the base field. For the special case of locally-complex Cayley--Dickson algebras over the reals, we prove that every such polynomial has a root. We prove the existence of right eigenvalues for any $2 \times 2$ matrix over Cayley's octonions (the real octonion division algebra), and our root-finding method allows the computation of some of the right eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Adam Chapman, Ilan Levin, Solomon Vishkautsan

item.title: Quasi-equivalence of relabeled positroid cluster structures
item.description: arXiv:2609.30637v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the Fraser--Sherman-Bennett conjecture on the quasi-equivalence of positroid cluster structures arising from admissibly relabeled plabic graphs. We construct a tilting module from the boundary necklace and obtain a Frobenius categorification of the relabeled cluster structure. By identifying localized characters of rank-one modules with Pl\"ucker coordinates, we match the stable images of the mutable face modules with the summands of a reachable cluster-tilting object in the stable category. The induced derived equivalence yields a unimodular transformation of relative index lattices intertwining the full extended exchange matrices. These comparisons show that the identity map on the coordinate ring is a quasi-cluster isomorphism between the two cluster structures.
item.dc:creator: Yilin Wu
